title: Bash prompt's 'don't ask again for: git mv *, +2 more' hides which rules it will save (here sed -i rules)
observed: kiln defect (UX). Prompt for 'cd "$PWD" && mkdir -p … && git mv … && sed -i '' 's/^package main$/package store/' … && sed -i '' … && ls -R internal' offered '2  Yes, and don't ask again for: git mv *, +2 more'. The two hidden rules are persistent allow rules written to .kiln/settings.local.json, and at least one is an in-place sed that rewrites files. The user cannot see them before agreeing, and the prompt has room for a second line.
expected: List every rule the option will save (wrapping to more rows), or let Tab or a key expand the list before confirming.

fix.note: 7c2dfff on branch worktree-agent-ae1e528c60b007fe6 (not merged): every rule is named, one per row when they do not fit; no real-terminal re-drive
